product.title: Risk, Volatility & Rational Aggression
product.summary: Three seasons testing whether a team's risk-taking matches its situation.
product.whatStudentsDo: Students pick a team whose circumstances differ — a legacy power, a small-market reset, a cash-rich expansion side — commit to a strategy from stability to boom-or-bust, then run three seasons of drafting, trading and free agency under the cap. Scoring weights whether the risk taken fitted the context, not whether it paid off.
product.technology: React + TypeScript + Zustand, deployed by GitHub Actions to Pages

studentDataProfile.notes: State kept in browser localStorage only; no server call observed.

governance.maturityBasis: A complete state machine and scoring model, deployed by CI, but visibly unpolished. No student-run evidence exists.

health.technicalBasis: Playtested end to end 2026-08-16. The richest simulation in the account: stochastic seasons, enforced cap constraints, and scoring that tracks the moves actually made rather than the strategy label chosen. Two defects, one of which misleads on the concept being taught.
knownBlockers: The dashboard contradicts the rest of the game on the core lesson: it tells the player their team should AVOID risk while the onboarding modal, team select and risk-context card all say the same team SHOULD take risks.
The final score prints an unrounded float (43.666666666666664).

curation.tierBasis: The richest simulation in the account: stochastic seasons, enforced cap constraints, and scoring that reads the moves actually made rather than the strategy label chosen. The dashboard that told every team to play it safe was repaired in this pass.

openQuestions: A 1,042-line implementation plan describes a Postgres and Redis backend that was never built; the shipped app is entirely client-side. Its stated 20–30 minute session is a planning target, not a measurement, so no duration is recorded.
